newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul prosecutors probe bankers over loan scandal.
newsitem.headline: Seoul prosecutors probe bankers over loan scandal.

text.p: South Korean state prosecutors said they were questioning heads of two leading local banks and a former president of a state bank on Tuesday over a loan scandal surrounding insolvent Hanbo Steel Co.
They are Sheen Kwang-shik of Korea First Bank, Woo Chan-mok of Cho Hung Bank and Lee Hyung-koo, former chief of the state-run Korea Development Bank.
"The three were summoned today and are now being questioned at the prosecution office," senior prosecutor Choi Byung-koog told reporters.

Hanbo Steel, flagship of the Hanbo Group, the 14th largest conglomerate in South Korea, had accumulated about five trillion won ($5.8 billion) in loans from 61 banks and financial institutions before it was declared insolvent on January 23.
Prosecution officials said the bankers would be questioned on whether they received commissions in return for offering huge loans to Hanbo Steel, the country's second largest steelmaker.
Hanbo Group founder Chung Tae-soo was arrested by prosecutors over the loan scandal on Friday.
